The Family Asset Protection Checklist

What to list, look up and ask about while Dad is managing fine.

Download PDF

Dad is managing fine, and nothing has to be settled. You've started to wonder how his house and savings would be treated if he ever needed long-term care, and nobody in the family has a full list of what he owns. Check what you've done, at your family's own pace. Anything unchecked is something to get to when it's convenient. It says nothing about how any of it would be treated.

List

Look up

Ask about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you list, look up and ask. It doesn't tell you which of Dad's assets may be protected, how any of them would be treated, or whether anything should change. Rules vary by state and change, and those answers come from a professional who knows Dad's state. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You've listed what Dad owns, looked up whose name is on it and written down what to ask. The planning interview asks about your family's situation in order, including the parts a list doesn't reach, and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for care.

Where this comes from

The item marked 1 follows the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's guide for older homeowners, which says to seek advice from legal and tax professionals about transferring property. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
